label: prop:full-pole-structure-mass-trace
title: Cyclotomic expansion of the cleared mass trace
html:
Let T_w \in H_n(q) be a standard basis element, with the Markov trace at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and h = q - q^{-1}. Then:

  1. By the Hecke-algebra Markov-trace structure of V. F. R. Jones [jones1987], \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) is a polynomial in z of degree at most n-1 with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[h]. Hence the cleared numerator
  N(T_w) \;:=\; (q^{2}+1)^{\,n-1}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(T_w) \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].
  1. N(T_w) lies in the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} := \varprojlim_m \mathbb{Z}[q]/((q;q)_m) of Kazuo Habiro [habiro2004cyclotomic] (applied to unified Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants in [habiro2008]), in which q is a unit, and expands cyclotomically as
  N(T_w)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{m \geq 0} a_m(T_w)\,(q; q)_m .
  1. The trace itself is not in general an element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. For T_w = \sigma_1 \in H_2(q), \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z satisfies (1+q^{2})\,z = q^{3}, and evaluating at q = i (a ring map \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[i]) would give 0 = -i.

The primitive roots of unity populate S^1 densely, blocking any complex-analytic continuation across the boundary. The Habiro ring provides the algebraic substrate for the cleared numerator, not for the trace: the factor (q^{2}+1)^{-(n-1)} has poles at q = \pm i, and only after removing it does evaluation at every root of unity make sense.
